result.title: Binary Discrete Diffusion: Candidate-Set Diffusion for Logic and Planning Tasks
result.summary: Discrete diffusion models iteratively denoise a noisy sequence of categorical data such as text, enabling any-order generation with self-correction and in-filling capabilities. This makes them promising candidates for reasoning, planning, and constrained-generation tasks like coding and math. Yet masked and uniform diffusion erase a token's identity in a single corruption event, so their noisy states cannot explicitly represent partially resolved uncertainty in which several alternatives remain plausible. We close this gap with Binary Discrete Diffusion, a family of continuous-time discrete-diffusion processes whose noisy state is a set of candidate tokens per position, represented as a binary membership vector. Binary diffusion changes candidate sets through additions and removals, allowing information to be lost and recovered gradually while the diffusion state itself represents partial uncertainty. On Sudoku-Extreme, Boxoban, and graph coloring, the symmetric formulation of binary diffusion consistently outperforms strong, well-tuned masked and uniform baselines under matched architectures and controlled training, sampling, and tuning budgets, with its largest gains on the hardest instances, while remaining competitive on language modeling (Text8, TinyStories, OpenWebText). These results support candidate sets as an effective intermediate representation for iterative reasoning and show that the corruption kernel can materially change the computation learned by the reverse model.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Binary Discrete Diffusion：用每个位置的候选 token 集合（二元隶属向量）作为含噪状态，通过连续时间离散扩散中的增删操作逐步恢复信息，在数独、Boxoban、图着色及语言建模上验证该状态表示优于 masked/uniform 扩散基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 候选集合作为「部分不确定性」的显式中间状态，可能为 LVR 中多假设 latent 状态的表示与迭代更新、以及扰动核如何塑造逆向计算提供可核查线索，但论文为纯文本任务，尚无视觉证据接入。
